newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent pushes lower in late trading.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent pushes lower in late trading.

text.p: April Brent crude futures in Asia pushed lower in late afternoon dealings on Friday, as bears put this week's low of $19.09 in their sights.
April Brent last traded on SIMEX at $19.20 per barrel, down 15 cents from London's settlement, after hitting an intraday low of $19.15.

Brokers said the weakness of NYMEX on ACCESS was undermining Brent. News of potential unrest in northern Iraqi Kurdish regions and Nigerian oil workers considering strike action, was not affecting trading, they said.
NYMEX April crude was last traded at $20.72 per barrel, down 17 cents from New York was being driven by the products.
The crude contract had seen offers in good size at $20.75, which might signal some resistance at that level intraday, before it fell to the intraday low and fresh six-month trough of $20.64.
"The rebound from $20.64 was quite weak," one broker said.

March heating oil, which expires later in New York, was last traded at 55.05 cents per gallon, down 0.98 cent, extending the 0.65 losses overnight. March gasoline, which firmed in New York, turned lower on ACCESS, last trading at 62.00, down 0.67.
